      - text: Show P(B | A)
      - paragraph: The reverse condition uses a different sample space.
    - article:
      - heading "Common Misconception" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Common Misconception
      - paragraph: P(A | B) and P(B | A) need not be equal.
      - paragraph: Order matters in conditional probability. Equality is possible for some event counts.
    - article:
      - heading "KEY TAKEAWAY" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: KEY TAKEAWAY
      - paragraph: Conditioning restricts the sample space. We measure the event only within the chosen condition.
      - paragraph: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)
      - text: Provided P(B) > 0.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: WORKED EXAMPLE
      - paragraph: "In a club of 40 students: A = chess (18), B = music (16), A ∩ B = 8. Find P(A | B)."
      - heading "Solution:" [level=3]
      - paragraph: P(A | B) = 8/16 = 1/2 = 0.5
    - article:
      - heading "Why this matters" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: Why this matters
      - paragraph: Conditional probability answers questions like “Among those who play music, how likely is it that a student plays chess?”
